title: School Schedule system
summary: A day contains multiple discrete class periods a player can choose to attend or skip; attending costs a time slot and rolls a skill check whose degree of success can grant bonuses, information, or an NPC contact on top of raising the kid's grade; skipping accrues toward a bad report card dealt with later. Each kid also picks one afterschool club, with GM-run content in the evening quarter.
description:
Explicitly speculative, recorded with the user's own tentative language preserved rather than tightened: a day contains multiple discrete class periods; attending one costs a time slot and rolls a skill check, and the degree of success can grant bonuses, information, or an important NPC contact, on top of raising the attending kid's grade. Skipping is explicitly permitted ('leave to avoid lessons') but accrues toward a bad report card, with consequences dealt with later rather than immediately. Design intent matches the existing Time Economy: there should always be more interesting things to do than slots to spend on them — school just adds another menu layered into the mandatory-school portion of the day rather than replacing it.

Ideas floated within this, also speculative: a History class as the natural (if optional) vector for campaign backstory, with the specific hope that at least one player attends it so the table gets the lore somehow without forcing it on everyone; after-hours clubs as a higher-commitment option on top of the class system; weekly objectives (separate from daily attendance) that grant bonuses or avoid penalties, also costing time slots.

Settled since: the school and the Directorate's facility are one campus on one island, with the military end to the north-west and the school further south-east (open-questions.json#school-facility-same-location; LEDGER #13).

ADDENDUM, 2026-09-13 (fun idea, recorded to the wishlist, not decided): Ingram's own framing — 'Characters should get to pick a single special afterschool club to be a part of. We run fun content in these for evening slots.' This gives the vague 'after-hours clubs' bullet above a concrete shape: ONE club per kid (not several), chosen as a standing pick rather than a per-day option, and it's specifically a vehicle for bespoke GM-run scenes rather than a passive stat bonus. Grounds cleanly in the Time Economy that already exists: data/campaign/config.json's four quarters are morning/afternoon/evening/night, school already occupies the mandatory morning+afternoon quarters, and evening is one of the four discretionary slices — so 'evening slots' likely means club night claims that quarter's slice on the days it runs.
sourceContext: User 'vibe with me' worldbuilding session — originally captured as prose in design/campaign-arc.md's 'Evolving mechanics threads' section, migrated here on audit.
openSubQuestions: Full class list and which skills each maps to — not designed.
Exact bonus/info/contact table per degree of success — not designed.
Report-card consequence mechanics — 'dealt with later' was explicitly left open by the user.

After-hours clubs — now a concrete floated shape (2026-09-13): one club per kid, GM-run content in the evening quarter. Still open: what clubs actually exist, whether club night competes with the evening quarter's other discretionary options (rest, investigation, Frame modification, etc.) or is exempt from that competition, whether the club choice is permanent or can change later, and what mechanical vs. purely narrative shape the 'fun content' takes.
